newsitem.title: USA: Scotsman sees Kysor acquisition accretive.
newsitem.headline: Scotsman sees Kysor acquisition accretive.

text.p: Scotsman Industries Inc said Monday it expects Kysor, which it acquired in March 1997, will be accretive to earnings per share in the second half of this year and for the full year.
Earlier, Scotsman reported second quarter net earnings of $7.1 million, even with a year ago.
Earlier, Scotsman reported second quarter net income of $7.1 million, even with a year ago.

"Despite continuing softness in Europe, we are on track with Wall Street's estimates and our own expectations for the second quarter," Richard Osborne, chairman, said in a statement. "The Kysor business, which was acquired in March of this year and which will shift Scotsman's historical pattern of earnings more to the second half of the year, contributed $73 million in revenues in the second quarter, an increase of nine percent over Kysor's pro forma revenues for the second quarter of 1996."
Scotsman said its Delfield unit's sales performance was encouraging, with food preparation and storage equipment revenues up 15 percent over the comparable quarter last year.

"However, the unit's progress at improving profitability lags behind our expectations," Osborne said. "Slowing of expansion plans by Boston Market (Boston Chicken Inc ), one of Delfield's major customers, will likely impact sales in the near term."
